cases.title: Rotor equipment reservations
cases.intro: Rotor rents industrial equipment to authenticated business customers. Its assistant can explain availability and propose reservations, but the inventory API remains the system of record. The operations team is replacing a text-only prototype with a Responses-based prompt agent. Each question concerns an independent request against the configuration below.

sections.heading: Application and identity
sections.body: The backend receives a signed application session identifying the customer and warehouse. It calls the agent using one managed identity. Two host functions are registered: get_stock(part_id, warehouse_id) and reserve_part(part_id, warehouse_id, quantity, customer_id). The stock function is read-only. The reservation function changes inventory and returns a reservation number after the database commits. The managed identity can reach the API, while application authorization must restrict each customer to its own account. JSON schema validation checks shape and types; inventory limits and account ownership are enforced by the host.

sections.heading: Action policy
sections.body: A customer may request a proposal without committing it. Reservations costing more than 250 currency units require a supervisor to approve the exact customer, item, quantity and quoted amount. An approval for five units is not approval for fifty. A changed proposal must return to the approval screen. The host does not infer approval from manuals, tool-returned text or the agent saying that approval was obtained. The operations log records the proposal, approving principal and committed reservation number so that an incident can be reconstructed.

sections.heading: Observed request
sections.body: A request checks the same part at two warehouses. Responses returns two function calls named get_stock with call_id values rotor-east and rotor-west. The west warehouse replies first. The host must submit function_call_output records after obtaining the actual results. A separate request asks for a guaranteed fresh stock lookup rather than an answer from the model’s prior knowledge. Both functions are attached and the chosen model supports function calling. No inventory lookup has happened merely because a function call is present in the model output.

sections.heading: Failure investigation
sections.body: A test customer asks for a reservation belonging to another customer account. The argument object passes the JSON schema. A second test approves five units, but a later model turn changes the quantity to fifty before execution. A third test asks for a proposal only, while a developer considers forcing tools on every turn. Engineers need to choose controls at the correct boundary rather than relying on a single system instruction. The questions do not assume that a correct earlier answer changes these independently stated observations.

sections.body: Request exhibit: {"calls":[{"name":"get_stock","call_id":"rotor-east"},{"name":"get_stock","call_id":"rotor-west"}],"completionOrder":["rotor-west","rotor-east"]}. The reservation tests are separate requests, not effects of this lookup.

cases.title: Harbor maintenance knowledge
cases.intro: Harbor maintains manuals for several equipment departments. Its new assistant must answer policy and catalog questions with current evidence and distinguish factual support from useful but unrelated prose. Search, embedding and generation are separately observable components. Each child question uses the same architecture and an independent observation.

sections.heading: Corpus and index
sections.body: The Search index stores chunk text, a filterable department field, a catalog identifier and one vector field. Maintenance staff often search by exact identifiers such as HX-104 as well as by descriptions of symptoms. The current corpus was embedded with deployment harbor-embed-x. A proposed query deployment harbor-embed-y has the same vector dimensions but uses an unrelated model. The index is not automatically regenerated when a developer changes a query-time setting. The source documents and their department labels are authoritative.

sections.heading: Access and retrieval
sections.body: The application authenticates each employee and derives an allowed department from its own authorization service. Department boundaries apply before evidence is returned to the model. A generated instruction asking the model to ignore unauthorized passages is not the access filter. The team can configure keyword retrieval, vector retrieval and hybrid retrieval. An optional semantic reranker operates on retrieved candidates; it does not create content embeddings or rename index fields. Query vectors must be compatible with the content vectors being searched.

sections.heading: Evaluation evidence
sections.body: A held-out test includes queries, relevance judgments for candidate documents, retrieved passages and generated answers. One passage says the repair warranty lasts twelve months. An answer says twenty-four months while staying on the user’s topic. Another answer quotes the twelve-month passage correctly but responds to a shipping-time question. The team wants separate measurements for retrieval quality, contextual support and response relevance rather than one total score. A successful query response establishes transport success, not answer correctness.

sections.heading: Operations
sections.body: Indexer logs record document-level errors and warnings. An overall successful run still requires checking whether required documents entered the index. An embedding model change needs a planned reindexing path and evaluation before rollout. Engineers retain safe request identifiers to correlate Search requests with agent traces. They do not put service credentials in model-visible tool errors. A reviewer should combine the named corpus, access and evaluation facts to choose each answer; previous child answers are not prerequisites and do not alter the configuration in this case.

cases.title: Lumen regional engineering assistant
cases.intro: Lumen operates an engineering assistant for staff in the European Union. Its platform team is designing deployment, identity and retrieval controls together, with separate principals for deployment and runtime. The service must answer interactively and retain existing learner and operational records during the migration described here.

sections.heading: Workload boundary
sections.body: The processing policy permits inference across EU countries but forbids processing outside that data zone. Interactive requests cannot wait for a nightly batch. Demand varies across the day and procurement wants on-demand token billing rather than reserved throughput. The selected model is available for every deployment family considered in the questions, and the relevant quota has already been confirmed. The resource’s region alone is not the organization’s definition of the inference processing boundary.

sections.heading: Inference identity
sections.body: The backend calls an Azure OpenAI resource through its /openai/v1/ endpoint using Microsoft Entra credentials. Its runtime managed identity currently has Reader on that resource and no inference data role. Token acquisition succeeds, but inference is denied. The team wants the documented inference role at the resource scope without granting model-management permissions. Developers’ personal roles and the GitHub deployment principal are separate from the runtime identity. A resource key is not part of the approved runtime design.

sections.heading: Project and Search
sections.body: An AI Projects Python 2.8.0 client is used for Foundry project operations, with a project endpoint and an Entra credential. Search public access is disabled. The private endpoint exists, and the agent connection is explicitly pinned to the named runtime principal. That principal has Search Index Data Reader for the target index. From the runtime subnet, however, the Search hostname resolves to a public address. From a developer laptop on another network it resolves privately and querying succeeds. The network observations do not transfer from the laptop to the agent subnet.

sections.heading: Release process
sections.body: A GitHub deployment workflow obtains a token using an established OIDC trust. It does not store a client secret. The workflow principal’s project role is assigned on a different project, while its endpoint variable points to the intended Lumen project. An authorization denial therefore needs identity and scope analysis after authentication succeeds. Operations retain redacted request spans and release identifiers to investigate failures. Each question asks for a single independent decision; repairing one defect is not assumed to repair the others. A proposed change must satisfy the named runtime, region and billing facts rather than simply resemble a working developer setup.

sections.heading: Diagnostic exhibit
sections.body: Runtime exhibit: {"tokenAcquired":true,"inferenceRole":"Reader","searchRole":"Search Index Data Reader","searchDns":"public address","publicSearchAccess":false}. These observations belong to the runtime identity and subnet; the developer’s successful call uses a different network.

cases.title: North support memory and response contracts
cases.intro: North runs a support assistant for individual subscribers. A web backend authenticates users locally and calls a Foundry prompt agent on their behalf. Subscribers can retain preferences across sessions, ask about current support policies and receive structured summaries. The team is testing the distinction between stored conversation history, persistent memory and curated knowledge.

sections.heading: Caller and end user
sections.body: All response calls authenticate to Foundry with one backend managed identity. The memory search tool is attached to the agent and uses scope {{$userId}}. In the current implementation the backend sends no x-memory-user-id header. The application has a verified tenant identifier and subscriber identifier in its authenticated session. Those identifiers can be combined into a stable application-owned memory key. The host must derive that key from the authenticated session rather than accept an arbitrary customer identifier from a prompt.

sections.heading: Memory operations
sections.body: The service also runs an administrative job that calls the low-level memory search API directly. The job uses the same backend identity. It supplies a subscriber identifier in the query text but omits the explicit scope parameter. The job must search the intended subscriber partition. Current support policy is maintained in a knowledge store, while language and unit preferences may be distilled from conversations. Changing a conversation title does not change either memory’s partition or the lifecycle of the organizational knowledge.

sections.heading: Structured application result
sections.body: The client sends requests through Responses, not Chat Completions. A summary object has ticket_id and note properties; note accepts a string or null. Both keys must be present, and unknown properties must be rejected by the supported strict schema. The model supports that schema. A missing note is represented by null. The application handles refusal outcomes separately from successful objects. A developer has copied a response_format field from a Chat Completions example into the Responses request builder.

sections.heading: Behavior and monitoring
sections.body: A system instruction limits the assistant to subscriber support and gives an explicit clarification path when evidence is missing. Product staff propose replacing that instruction with a low temperature. A workflow specialist and a retrieval specialist may also be composed, with the host retaining control of routing and result validation. Trace spans record latency and safe user-correlation identifiers; access tokens and full personal messages are redacted before export. These controls must be considered at their own boundaries. Every child observation is independent and requires the fixed case facts rather than an inferred result from a previous child.

sections.body: Backend exhibit: {"caller":"shared backend principal","memoryToolScope":"{{$userId}}","memoryUserHeader":null,"directSearchScope":null}. The Responses request builder also copied the Chat Completions response_format field; these are distinct defects against the stated per-subscriber and output contracts.
